summary: No trades today and nine thesis_updates. Equity closed at $625.09 (day -$1.21, about -0.19%, against SPY's value about -0.36%), and drawdown is 1.74%. Since version 6 started on 11-10 the agent is +0.41%, against shadow -0.47% and SPY +0.96%. Standing aside on buys was forced, not chosen: cash was only about $2 above the 10% buffer, and no sell proposals came. The decision was sound as process. It took the Skeptic's WMT and VNQ cases seriously and acted on them where it could: it raised WMT's stop to $119, close to breakeven, asked the Proposer for a one-third trim, and restated VNQ on its remaining merits. The L6 cleanups (re-dated SPY 200-day, INCY stop measured from the fill, unmeasurable XLV clauses dropped, weight figures removed) all went into stored theses. No stop tripped at the close. The close stop blocks show BND NEAR at +0.93% (mark 70.65 against 70.00) and IEF NEAR at +0.79% (90.21 against 89.50). Both bond sleeves lost about 0.6-0.8% on a day SPY also fell. So both closed about half as far from their stops as the +1.6% the decision quoted, and they did so on the exact correlation the Market Analyst had flagged. The weakest part of the reasoning was defending IEF as 'a small hedge for an equity drawdown' on the same morning the Market Analyst said duration is not hedging and bonds are falling with stocks. That role was contradicted by evidence the PM had in hand, and today's close repeated the contradiction. Everything else checks out at the close. VOO and VTI are +3.91% above the SPY 200-day line (SPY 757.12 against 728.65). WMT is +6.04% above the new $119 stop going into its unconfirmed ~11-19 print, and a close-based stop still can't protect against a gap. VNQ is +4.83% above $92. IDXX is +9.07% above $640. The single names (CARG, DPZ, FAST, INCY, KR, MSCI, VRSN) are all 10% or more above their stops. The qualitative clauses had no new trigger in today's notes.

broken_theses.why: Not tripped (stop block +0.79% above $89.50), but its stated role is broken. Today's decision kept IEF as 'a small hedge for an equity drawdown', while the Market Analyst's note said bonds are falling with stocks after the hot CPI. On the close it fell 0.84% while SPY fell. The thesis already calls it low-conviction and 'first bond to cut', and the stop is now within one ordinary rates day. Tomorrow it should either get a role that today's bond-equity correlation does not contradict or be proposed for sale, so it is not left for a noise-level stop to decide.

Not tripped (stop block +0.93% above $70.00). The 'low-vol ballast' premise is weakened, though, for the same reason as IEF: BND fell 0.62% on a down-equity day and is 0.62% below its 200-day per the Market Analyst. Its second clause can't fire while he is risk-off, so in practice the $70 stop is the only live exit. That stop sits about 1.8% under the fill, close to the noise-level spacing L4 warns against for a sleeve whose job is to be steady.

Not tripped (stop block +4.83%), but the original thesis is gone, as the PM acknowledged: the Market Analyst dropped Real Estate from favor and his risk-off stance has already met one leg of the clause. It is now held on residual merits only, and the TLT leg (2.23% below its 200-day as of 11-11, 3% trigger) is the next exit. If no cut is proposed, it is a token sleeve with no stated reason, which L4 warns against.

lessons: Don't give a holding a role, such as 'hedge for an equity drawdown', that the Market Analyst's same-day evidence contradicts. If bonds are falling with stocks, a bond sleeve needs a different stated reason or a sell request; keeping the old role leaves the exit to a stop that is only noise away.

When the PM agrees a Skeptic sizing case is serious but has no proposal to trade, raising the stop and asking for the trim was the right move. Tomorrow's PM should check whether the Proposer actually brought the WMT trim before the estimated ~11-19 print, and should say so explicitly if it didn't. A close-based stop does not cover gap risk.

Bond stops set about 2% under the fill can trip on ordinary rate moves while a 25bp-vs-50bp FOMC debate is live. When a stop goes NEAR, decide on purpose whether to let it trip (and say so) or to re-anchor it through thesis_updates for a stated reason, rather than carrying it unchanged.

A risk-off stance with an unchanged book is defensible only when cash and the absence of proposals force it, as they did today. On those days, name the first sleeves to cut (today: VNQ, then IEF) so the Proposer can bring sells on the next run.
